# C10 — Mediation / Pramāṇa

## #0

**Pramāṇa is Objective Internality as means**, between Subjective Immediacy as knower and World as known; Life / Mind is the whole relation. [Objective Internality](C41-Objective-Internality.md) names the constituted interior through which a world becomes available. Mediation specifies how this disclosure occurs: what becomes salient, what transformations it undergoes, and how the disclosed can be known and acted upon.

The means participates in the determination of its object. A recollection presents an event as past; a perception presents what is being encountered; a testimony carries another's account. Their difference can matter even when the resulting sentence is identical. Knowledge does not require the means to vanish. It requires an adequate relation to what is known through it. The [immutable gap](C05-Immutable-Gap.md) makes that relation necessary without abolishing its reality.

## #1

In [[symbolon/episteme/sources/indian-philosophy/dyczkowski/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration|Dyczkowski’s Śaiva discussion]], pp.63–64, subject, object and means attend one cognitive act together. The means is not a neutral addition inserted after an independently complete subject and object have been established. Their differentiation belongs to the one act whose articulation makes an object available.

The three luminaries preserve that relation as an image. The Sun figures the illuminating means, the Moon the object shining by reflected light, and Fire the subject which takes the perceived into itself. The illuminating Sun, reflected Moon and assimilating Fire belong to one cognitive scene. Remove the means and the account loses the act of disclosure; remove the knower and it loses the act's first-person fact; remove the known and it loses what the act differentiates. The image teaches their relation rather than presenting three self-sufficient things.

## #2

The relation must preserve the difference it renders intelligible. Dyczkowski's pp.65–66 press this through colour: if consciousness were entirely homogeneous in its knowing, blue and yellow could not appear as distinct. Formless availability and determinate appearance must be thought together. At pp.70–72, the distinction between a mirror or crystal and conscious reflexivity adds an active power of recognition, memory and presentation to the account. A mechanically reflected appearance does not by itself supply that whole operation.

Illumination makes an appearance available; [reflexive awareness](../A05-Prakasa-Vimarsa.md) recognises, retains and returns upon what appears. The epistemic middle has an active office: it selects, discloses, retains and presents. Remembering an earlier perception does not simply repeat the earlier event, because its relation to time has changed. The means participates in that change while retaining what makes this a recollection of that event.

## #3

A symbol makes the same demand on an account. In [[symbolon/episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-definition-god-draft3/taylor-2026-definition-god-draft3|Taylor’s magnet image]], iron filings form a visible pattern through a relation whose source the pattern does not contain. The partial expression lets an unavailable whole become intelligible without becoming that whole’s exhaustive inventory. The visible pattern makes the relation to an uncontained condition encounterable.

A determinate sign fixes something; a living symbol carries that determination in a relation exceeding it. Through [diaphaneity](C09-Diaphaneity.md), the shaping conditions become readable within the appearance. In [speech](../A06-Vak.md), formative power becomes mental articulation and utterance which an addressee can answer. Feeling, perception, intention, contact and attention also disclose a world; mediation therefore remains active before a fully formed verbal statement.

## #4

Suppose the sentence is “the door is locked.” Seeing the bolt engaged, recalling that it was locked yesterday, and repeating another person's report can produce the same words. They expose different routes of correction. Renewed perception can discover that the bolt has moved; a dated record can disclose that the recollection concerns yesterday rather than now; tracing testimony can identify who checked and when. The sentence does not carry these distinctions on its surface, but they change the reason for accepting it and the action it warrants.

The example makes the difference between source, means and warrant concrete. A generated answer drawn from a record and a conjecture about an unobserved state cannot exchange authority simply because they sound alike. Returning through the means requires recovering the source relation and the transformation that made this answer available.

At the local comparison, the judging agent is the functional knower; the dated report, current observation, memory, comparison rule and available tools are means; the differentiated door-states and proposed actions are known. The agent actually determines which claim is warranted through those means. In the containing person’s inquiry, that whole checking apparatus can itself serve as means: its judgment is received, questioned and used in deciding what to do. Further inspection can make the judging centre known without turning the present condition of appearing into one more item in its inventory.

The [Sanskrit enumeration case](../../../symbolon/episteme/etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES-symbol-account-and-trust.md#sanskrit-enumeration-and-discriminative-practice) historicises a particular taxonomy: Sāṃkhya Kārikās 4–6 distinguish perception, inference and trustworthy testimony. The Śaiva source above concerns the co-presence of knower, means and known; this Sāṃkhya case supplies its own account of valid cognition. The essay's broader appointment of Objective Internality to the office of means preserves, rather than erases, such differences of warrant.

An [[symbolon/episteme/etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/WHOLE-FIELD|account answers to source]] by retaining how its claim was formed and allowing the counterpart to correct or refuse it. The [appointed bearer](C29-Mediating-Office-Derivative-Sovereignty.md) can exercise real discretion within a commission. Authority to convey or act upon a report remains different from having originated the event it reports.

## #5→0

The return reaches the condition implicated by the encounter. [A corrected result and a revised criterion](../A31-Deferential-Intelligence.md) do different work: another answer can be adequate under a sound rule, while a defective rule requires a change in what counts as adequate. A system could keep recommending that the supposedly locked door be avoided while consulting the same outdated record. Retrieving a current observation changes the available evidence; changing a rule that treats old observations as current changes how the means will work next time. Those are different, consequential repairs.

An answerable mediation preserves a route to its sources and governing criteria. A current observation can correct the answer or model under a fitting rule; a failed rule, permission or commission reaches the authority able to change it. A challenged condition can also be retained for an answerable reason. The next act inherits the corrected judgment or reasoned retention together with the source and circumstance that warranted it. Merely recording disagreement leaves this consequence unperformed.

[Trust and faith](C48-Trust-Faith-under-Formal-Limit.md) act through this relation without waiting for complete possession of its source. The [context frame](C08-Context-Context-Frame.md) situates the act, and [diaphaneity](C09-Diaphaneity.md) lets its shaping conditions become readable. What is learned through a means can then renew the means itself.
